prompt:
Design a dense, professional single-page infrastructure monitoring screen called 'Routing topology'. It is an operations tool for one person watching LLM spend, not a marketing page. Light background, high information density, tabular numerals, monospace for model identifiers.

LAYOUT: a left-to-right layered flow diagram with exactly four columns, each with a small uppercase column header: 'CALLERS', 'TIERS', 'MODELS', 'UPSTREAM'. Nodes are compact rounded rectangles stacked vertically in each column, ordered by traffic descending. Column position alone tells you the node type, so do not color-code node types. Curved bezier edges connect Caller to Tier, Tier to Model, and Model to the single Upstream node at far right. Edge thickness encodes request volume.

NODE CONTENT: each node card shows a bold name on line one, and on line two small grey stats: request count, cost in dollars, and token counts. Tier nodes additionally show a small badge for the data-governance gate, e.g. 'zdr' in green or 'deny' in amber, and an optional 'floor 8192' chip. Example caller names: coordinator, xxpress, financebot, rise, openhuman, benchmark. Example tier names: fast, balanced, deep, free, jev. Example model names: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, z-ai/glm-flash-latest, minimax/minimax-m3, qwen/qwen3.7-max, qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free. Upstream node is a single card labelled openrouter.ai.

EDGE STATES, each must be distinguishable without color: healthy primary route is a solid green line with a filled dot glyph; a fallback that carried traffic is a dashed amber line with an arrow glyph; a link with failures is a thick solid rose line with a cross glyph and a small red count; a declared route with zero traffic is a thin dotted grey line with an open circle. Every edge carries a tiny direct label showing request count and cost.

HEADER BAR: title on the left, then a window selector (last 24 hours / today / last 7 days / last 200 requests), an auto-refresh toggle, and a row of summary chips on the right: '1,376 requests', '$12.38', '9 callers / 10 models'. Anomaly chips render with a red outline: 'no governance gate: jev', 'served off declared chain: qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902'.

DETAIL PANEL: when a node is selected, a right-hand drawer slides in showing the node name, kind, requests, cost, input and output tokens, its governance gate as JSON, and a list of inbound and outbound links each with request count, cost, p50 latency and failure count.

LEGEND: a thin horizontal legend under the diagram showing the four edge states with their glyph, line style and color together.

FOOTER: a small grey note stating that only operational telemetry is shown and no prompt content is read.

STYLE RULES: no donut charts, no gradient fills, no decorative illustrations, no big rounded cards with drop shadows, no more than five accent hues, subtle 1px borders, tight 4px/8px spacing rhythm, everything aligned to a grid. It should look like a Grafana or Datadog topology view built by a careful engineer, readable at 100 percent zoom on a 1440px wide screen without horizontal scrolling.
